chapters.title: Chapter 5: Claiming Your TDS Credit and Refund

lessons.title: Checking Your TDS Credits in Form 26AS and AIS

body.text: TDS only counts if it reaches your PAN. Your payslips and bank statements prove tax was cut. Your tax credit statement proves it was deposited and reported. Before filing, check every rupee against the statement, not against your own records.

children.text: Kavita, 38, a project manager in Hyderabad, also runs weekend workshops for a training company and holds FDs and a few dividend shares. Her records show ₹1,18,200 of TDS for the year. When she opened her tax credit statement in June, only ₹1,13,700 was showing as final credit, and there was an entry from a builder she had never heard of. This lesson shows how to read the statement, what each status means, and how to reconcile it with your own records before you file.

markDefs.definition: The Annual Information Statement under Section 510 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 and Rule 245 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026. It replaces Form 26AS and consolidates TDS, TCS, tax payments, high-value transactions, demands and refunds against a PAN.

body.title: Fill in the Blank: The Status You Want
body.textWithBlank: Before claiming a TDS credit in your return, confirm that its booking status is ___.
body.explanation: F means the tax reported against your PAN has been matched with an actual deposit. Credits showing U or O may not be allowed when your return is processed, even though the tax was deducted from you.

body.title: Kavita: TDS in her records vs final credit in the statement

children.text: Salary and bank TDS match perfectly. The training company has reported only ₹9,000 of the ₹12,000 it deducted, which usually means its January to March statement has not been filed or processed. The ₹1,500 of dividend TDS is there but unmatched. Together that is a ₹4,500 gap to chase before filing.

body.title: Try It: What Can Kavita Safely Claim Today?
body.prompt: If Kavita filed today, how much TDS could she claim with confidence, counting only entries in her statement with status F?
body.explanation: Only final credits count: ₹97,500 from her employer, ₹7,200 from HDFC Bank and ₹9,000 from the training company, totalling ₹1,13,700. Claiming the unmatched ₹1,500 or the unreported ₹3,000 risks those amounts being disallowed when her return is processed, which would turn into a tax demand.

body.title: Quick Check: The Stranger's Entry
body.question: Kavita's statement also shows ₹2,000 of TDS on commission paid by a Pune builder she has never dealt with. What should she do?
options: Claim it, since it is reported against her PAN
Not claim it, and submit feedback in AIS that the transaction is not related to her
Ask the builder to pay her the commission
body.explanation: The builder has almost certainly typed a wrong PAN, which is hers. The income is not hers, so she must not claim the credit or report the commission. She should use the feedback option in AIS to flag it as not related to her. The TDS really belongs to someone else, whose credit is missing, and the builder will need to correct its statement.

body.text: Notice the pattern in the last column. Almost every TDS credit problem can only be fixed by the deductor. You cannot edit your statement yourself, and AIS feedback flags a problem but does not create a missing credit. Your job is to spot problems early and chase the right person. Lesson 3 of this chapter covers exactly how.

children.text: Feedback does not change your TDS credit by itself, but it creates a record that you flagged the problem, and the department may seek confirmation from the reporting source. The exact wording of the options can differ slightly on the portal, so read them before choosing.

body.title: Scenario: The Missing Fourth Quarter
body.scenario: In early June 2027, Kavita sees that the training company has reported only ₹9,000 of the ₹12,000 it deducted from her ₹1,20,000 of workshop fees. Her invoices and bank statement show every payment was 10% short.
body.prompt: What is the most likely reason, and how should Kavita handle it before the filing deadline?
body.modelAnswer: The most likely reason is that the company's January to March 2027 statement, due by 31 May 2027, has not yet been filed or processed, so the last ₹3,000 has not reached her PAN. She should email the company's accounts team with her invoice numbers, the dates and amounts paid, and ask for the quarterly Form 131 certificate for January to March, which can only be generated once a correct statement is filed. She should check her statement again after a couple of weeks. If the credit appears with status F before she files, she claims the full ₹12,000. If the deadline is close and it still has not appeared, she can file on time claiming what is reflected, then revise her return once the credit shows. She should keep her invoices and bank statements as proof that tax was actually deducted.

body.title: Reconcile TDS Before You File
steps: List every payer that deducted TDS from you this year, with the amounts from payslips, invoices and certificates
Download your statement (Form 26AS and AIS for 2025-26, Form 168 from tax year 2026-27)
Match each deductor by name and TAN, and compare gross amount and TDS
Check that every credit you plan to claim shows status F
Flag entries that are not yours using AIS feedback, and do not claim them
For missing or unmatched credits, contact the deductor at least a few weeks before the filing deadline

body.label: Annual Information Statement, e-Filing Portal
body.description: Log in with your PAN and open the Annual Information Statement to view TDS credits, their status, and to submit feedback on incorrect entries.

cards.definition: Annual Information Statement from tax year 2026-27, under Section 510 and Rule 245, replacing Form 26AS and consolidating AIS.
Final. The deductor's reported TDS matches an actual deposit. Safe to claim.
Provisional. Reported by a government deductor, awaiting payment verification.
Unmatched. Challan details in the deductor's statement do not match a deposit.
Overbooked. The deductor claimed more against a challan than was deposited.
Your response to an entry in the statement, used to flag wrong, duplicate or unrelated transactions. It does not create missing credits.

points: Your TDS credit is what appears against your PAN in the department's statement, not what your payslips or invoices show
For income earned up to March 2026 check Form 26AS and AIS. From tax year 2026-27, check Form 168, which merges them
Match every deductor by name, TAN, gross amount and TDS, and claim only credits with status F
Status U means unmatched challan details and O means overbooking. Both need the deductor to act
Missing fourth-quarter credits are common in early June because those statements are due only by 31 May
Never claim TDS that is not yours. Flag it through AIS feedback, and chase deductors early for anything missing
